source.title: Interpretability Without Tradeoffs: Disentangling Polysemanticity At Equal Predictive Performance
source.authors: Dogukan Bagci; B. Schiele; Simone Schaub-Meyer; Jonas Fischer; Robin Hesse

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-initialization similarity of SAE dictionaries, bearing on the stability component of V5, and reports substantially different results across methods. It does not test superposition or its proposed causes.
record.gate_note: Table 4 reports cross-initialization dictionary similarity for SAE methods and ELUDe; these stability results bear on V5. Interpretability, accuracy, reconstruction, efficiency, steering, and other dictionary-geometry results do not test the listed claim versions and are not rows. Table 7's random-grouping control concerns interpretability gains, not these claim versions.
record.test_reason: A method paper (ELUDe). Its Table 4 directly measures cross-initialization stability of eight SAE/transcoder dictionaries on DINOv2-B/14. Several show low stability, which bears on the 'stable' part of V5 in a vision setting. No result bears on superposition itself (V1, V2, V3, V6) or on LLMs (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. More precisely: ELUDe decomposes polysemantic units into more interpretable subunits while exactly preserving model outputs. It often beats SAEs and transcoders on interpretability and is more stable than them. The paper does not draw conclusions about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces ELUDe, which clusters attribution patterns and restructures weights in vision models; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method or measure sparse-feature superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-initialization similarity differs substantially across dictionary methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Polysemantic neurons in vision transformers split into subunits driven by distinct upstream-unit contribution clusters (qualitative, plus MS-Score gains over a random grouping).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemantic neurons in vision models are composed of separable upstream-circuit groups recoverable without training.

record.problems: For the claim-relevant stability result, the study evaluates one vision backbone/configuration and uses cross-initialization cosine similarity as a stability proxy. It does not test completeness or canonicality of SAE features.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4 effective-rank and coherence values are omitted because they do not directly test any listed version. Other interpretability, faithfulness, generalization, efficiency, steering, and ablation outcomes likewise do not measure the listed claims.

untested.parts: Completeness and canonicality of SAE features; stability in language models; stability across seeds of the token dataset (only the initialization seed was varied).
All parts; there is no toy-model or sparsity experiment.
All parts; polysemanticity is attributed to superposition only by citation.
All parts; the experiments use vision models, not LLMs.

record.verdict_notes: The SAE stability numbers are baseline comparators in a method paper, measured in a vision setting (DINOv2-B/14) on one layer and one configuration. The Table 4 caption and Section B.3 describe the averaging protocol slightly differently. Section B.3 says training used the same seeded token dataset and only the initialization seeds varied.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features outnumber dimensions, overlap as nearly orthogonal directions, and show sparsity-dependent transitions or regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity, or important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or is evidence for superposition.
Whether LLM activations spread features across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features in LLMs.
The study measures cross-initialization stability of SAE dictionaries, but does not test their completeness or whether their features are canonical model units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

relationships.reason: Hungarian-matched cross-init similarity is only 13.32% and 13.38%: dictionaries largely differ across seeds (r1, r3).
relationships.display_finding: Hungarian-matched cross-initialization similarity was only 13.32% and 13.38%, so the dictionaries largely differed across seeds.

relationships.display_finding: Stability ranged from 50.77% to 86.85% depending on the SAE variant, and no variant was fully stable across seeds.
